title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 419
paragraphs: Having said this and having unbent the bow, he delivered it to those who had come. Then he took the purple garment and asked what it was and how it had been made. When the Ichthyophagoi told him the truth about the purple-fish and the dyeing of the fabric, he said that the men were deceitful and so were their garments. Next he asked about the twisted gold of the collar and the bracelets, and when the Ichthyophagoi explained how they were fashioned, the king burst into laughter and said, supposing them to be fetters, that in his country they had stronger fetters than these. Thirdly he asked about the perfumed ointment, and when they told him how it was made and how it was used for anointing, he said the same as he had said about the garment. Then when he came to the wine, and learned how it was made, he was exceedingly delighted with the taste of the drink, and asked besides what food the king ate and what was the longest time a Persian man lived. They told him he ate bread, explaining to him first how wheat was grown, and they said that eighty years was the longest term of life appointed for a Persian. In reply the Ethiopian said he did not wonder that they lived but a few years, when they fed on dung; for indeed they would not be able to live even as many years as this, if they did not renew their vigor with the drink — pointing to the wine — for in this respect, he said, his people were far behind the Persians.
